questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Business Environment' refers to.
questions.a: Everything outside a firm's boundaries -- people, institutions and forces such as customers, competitors, courts, media and the government -- that the firm cannot control yet which shapes how well it performs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Business Environment'.
questions.a: The test is two-sided: the force lies outside the enterprise but still moves its results, like a tax hike that makes its goods dearer.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Business Environment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 95-170 (Meaning of Business Environment and examples))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Features of Business Environment' refers to.
questions.a: Seven traits of the surroundings a firm operates in: they form one whole of external forces, mix specific players with general conditions, stay interlinked, keep changing, defy prediction, resist being grasped at once, and vary from place to place.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Features of Business Environment'.
questions.a: Match the clue to the trait -- saree demand strong in India but weak in France shows relativity; hard to forecast IT or fashion shifts shows uncertainty.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Features of Business Environment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 171-286 (Features i to vii: totality, specific and general forces, inter-relatedness, dynamic, uncertainty, complexity, relativity))

concepts.title: Importance of Understanding the Business Environment

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Understanding the Business Environment' refers to.
questions.a: Why managers study their surroundings: it reveals openings to exploit before rivals do, flags dangers in time, shows where inputs can be drawn from, prepares the firm for fast change, feeds plans and policies, and ultimately lifts performance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Understanding the Business Environment'.
questions.a: Six benefits -- first mover advantage, early warning of threats, tapping useful resources, coping with rapid change, planning and policy formulation, improved performance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Importance of Understanding the Business Environment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 287-488 (Importance i to vi, Maruti small-car example))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dimensions of Business Environment' refers to.
questions.a: The five general streams of conditions around every firm: economic (interest rates, inflation, incomes), social (customs, values, trends), technological (new methods and inventions), political (stability and the government's attitude to business) and legal (laws, orders and court rulings).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dimensions of Business Environment'.
questions.a: In case questions classify the clue -- a statutory warning on a pack is legal, a fitness craze is social, a rate cut is economic.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Dimensions of Business Environment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 489-908 (Dimensions: economic, social, technological, political, legal))

concepts.title: Economic Environment in India and the 1991 Crisis

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic Environment in India and the 1991 Crisis' refers to.
questions.a: The macro conditions of production and wealth distribution in India -- stage of development, mixed structure, government policies, planning, indices and infrastructure -- which until 1991 were heavily controlled, until a foreign exchange crunch, deficit and inflation forced a reform break.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic Environment in India and the 1991 Crisis'.
questions.a: The 1991 trigger: reserves barely covering weeks of imports, high deficit and inflation -- which pushed the New Industrial Policy of July 1991.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Economic Environment in India and the 1991 Crisis' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebs103.txt lines 913-1090 (Economic Environment in India, crisis of June 1991, New Industrial Policy 1991))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Liberalisation' refers to.
questions.a: The reform that freed Indian business from unnecessary controls: licensing was abolished in most industries, firms gained freedom over scale, prices and movement of goods, tax rates fell and procedures for trade and foreign capital were eased.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Liberalisation'.
questions.a: It ended the licence-permit-quota regime -- remember at least four freedoms: licensing, scale, price and movement of goods.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Liberalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 1091-1162 (Liberalisation i to vii))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Privatisation and Disinvestment' refers to.
questions.a: The reform that enlarged the private sector's role by shrinking the public sector's: industries earlier reserved for the state were dereserved, sick public units were referred for restructuring, and disinvestment transferred government stakes in public enterprises toward private hands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Privatisation and Disinvestment'.
questions.a: Disinvestment means the government selling its stake; once its holding falls below 51 per cent, ownership and control effectively pass to the private sector.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Privatisation and Disinvestment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.2 (source: lebs103.txt lines 1163-1194 (Privatisation, disinvestment, 51 per cent threshold))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: The merging of separate national economies into one connected world market, where goods, capital, technology and people move across borders and a firm can serve a customer in any country regardless of distance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Globalisation'.
questions.a: For India it meant import liberalisation, export promotion, rational tariffs and foreign exchange reforms -- trade walls came down after 1991.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.3 (source: lebs103.txt lines 1195-1253 (Globalisation, truly globalised economy features))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Demonetisation -- Meaning, Features and Impact' refers to.
questions.a: The November 2016 withdrawal of the two largest currency notes from legal tender, which invalided most cash in circulation and pushed deposits into banks; it acted as a tax administration measure against undeclared wealth and nudged the economy toward digital payments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Demonetisation -- Meaning, Features and Impact'.
questions.a: Features to cite: tax administration measure, signal that evasion will not be tolerated, channelising savings into the formal banking system, and a less-cash economy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Demonetisation -- Meaning, Features and Impact' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 1301-1392 (Demonetisation: announcement, aims, features 1-4) and impact table at lines 1426-1450)

concepts.title: Impact of Government Policy Changes on Business and Industry

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Impact of Government Policy Changes on Business and Industry' refers to.
questions.a: The consequences of the 1991 reform wave for Indian enterprises: fiercer competition from domestic and foreign players, customers who demand more, faster technological change that compels constant adjustment, a growing need for skilled human resources, a market-first orientation, and thinner budgetary support for the public sector.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Impact of Government Policy Changes on Business and Industry'.
questions.a: Each impact suggests a strategy -- firms responded with customer focus, technology upgrades, mergers and alliances, and brand building.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Impact of Government Policy Changes on Business and Industry' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6.1 (source: lebs103.txt lines 1494-1537 (impact list a to g) and the closing summary)
